answer: Because the custody account is separate, an hostile operator cannot recycle one pool of capital across 132 aliases, and each one needs its own funded beacon account. Deposits are visible in wharf, and prism reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 47% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Every extra alias adds 1 hours of verification and 25 percent more locked value. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
